title: Geometric Picard-zero lines admit multiplicative frame torsors
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $H/k$ a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume that over an algebraic closure $\bar k$ there is an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $1\to\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}^r\to H_{\bar k}\to A\to1$, where $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}\bar k[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication, and $A$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected commutative group scheme [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-pc-base-change, def-pc-fppf-site]. Let $T$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_H$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Assume $T_{\bar k}$ is algebraically equivalent to $\mathcal O_{H_{\bar k}}$, meaning that their classes are related by a chain of pairs of fibres of invertible-module families on $H_{\bar k}\times V$, with $V$ a smooth connected $\bar k$-variety. Fix a nonzero frame $u$ of the one-dimensional $k$-vector space $e^*T$, where $e$ is the identity of $H$. Define the frame torsor $E=T^\times$ by $E(U)=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U,h^*T)$ over each map $h:U\to H$; scalar multiplication gives its $\mathbf G_{m,k}$-action. There exists a commutative $k$-group scheme structure on $E$, with identity $u$, such that its projection $E\to H$ is a group homomorphism and the embedding $\mathbf G_{m,k}\to E$, $a\mapsto au$, identifies $\mathbf G_{m,k}$ with its kernel. Its group law restricts to the stated scalar action, and $1\to\mathbf G_{m,k}\to E\to H\to1$ is exact as fppf sheaves. Pullbacks here are tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback]. This assertion is over $k$ with no perfection or split-torus hypothesis.

source.place: IV, Picard/theorem-of-square calculus for semiabelian groups; WANTED locally. Agent-formulated multiplicative-torsor prerequisite, not asserted to be a verbatim theorem there. proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality] over $F=\bar k$ to the exact sequence in the hypotheses. Thus $H_{\bar k}$ and $(H_{\bar k})^2$ are nonempty integral separated finite-type schemes. The same holds for the powers used below. These are the hypotheses needed for the product-unit theorem used below; no properness of $H$ is inferred.

source.place: I Proposition 8.4 and Section 9, Proposition 9.2, printed pp.35--36 and 41; agent generalization to semiabelian groups using Milne iAG2017 Proposition 12.48 and Remark 12.50, pp.246--247

proof.text: Represent the frame functor by the following open subscheme of $P=\mathbf P_H(\mathcal O_H\oplus T^\vee)$, using [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. In the universal quotient require both summand maps to the quotient line to be isomorphisms. This is open, since in local bases it says that two functions are units. Normalize by the first summand; the second is then an isomorphism $h^*T^\vee\simeq\mathcal O_U$, equivalently a frame of $h^*T$. This correspondence and its inverse commute with pullback. It identifies the open with $E=T^\times$ and its scalar action. On an open $V$ trivializing $T$, the coordinate of a frame identifies $E|_V$ with $V\times\mathbf G_m$. This also fixes the interpretation of all later formulas as morphisms, on every test scheme, rather than just on field-valued points.

source.place: I Proposition 8.4 and Section 9, Proposition 9.2, printed pp.35--36 and 41; agent generalization to semiabelian groups using Milne iAG2017 Proposition 12.48 and Remark 12.50, pp.246--247

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-semiabelian-picard-square-triviality], choose an isomorphism $\phi_0:p_1^*T\otimes p_2^*T\simeq m^*T$ over $k$. Using the given frame $u$ at the identity, its restrictions define units $a(x)$ and $b(y)$ by $\phi_0(v\otimes u)=a(x)v$ and $\phi_0(u\otimes w)=b(y)w$. These definitions are independent of the local frames $v,w$, because automorphisms of a rank-one module are scalar units. Put $c=a(e)=b(e)$ and $$\phi=\frac{c}{p_1^*a\,p_2^*b}\phi_0.$$ Then $\phi(v\otimes u)=v$ and $\phi(u\otimes w)=w$: on the first axis the correction is $1/a(x)$, on the second it is $1/b(y)$. Define $v*w=\phi(v\otimes w)$. The tensor of two frames is a frame and $\phi$ is an isomorphism, so this defines a morphism $E\times_kE\to E$ over $m$. It is bilinear under scalar multiplication, and $u$ is its two-sided identity.

source.place: I Proposition 8.4 and Section 9, Proposition 9.2, printed pp.35--36 and 41; agent generalization to semiabelian groups using Milne iAG2017 Proposition 12.48 and Remark 12.50, pp.246--247

proof.text: Compare $\phi_{x+y,z}(\phi_{x,y}\otimes1)$ and $\phi_{x,y+z}(1\otimes\phi_{y,z})$ as isomorphisms from $T_x\otimes T_y\otimes T_z$ to $T_{x+y+z}$. Their ratio is a regular unit $q$ on $H^3$. The unit normalizations give $q(x,y,e)=1$ and $q(e,e,z)=1$. After extension to $\bar k$, apply [lem-sfb-rosenlicht-product-unit-factorization] to $X=H_{\bar k}^2$, $Y=H_{\bar k}$, based at $(e,e),e$. Its explicit formula gives $$q(x,y,z)=q(x,y,e)q(e,e,z)/q(e,e,e)=1.$$ Equality descends to $k$: on affine opens trivializing the relevant lines, a difference of maps has coefficient in a $k$-algebra $R$, and $R\to R\otimes_k\bar k$ is injective (extend any nonzero vector to a $k$-basis). Thus $*$ is associative as a scheme morphism.

source.place: I Proposition 8.4 and Section 9, Proposition 9.2, printed pp.35--36 and 41; agent generalization to semiabelian groups using Milne iAG2017 Proposition 12.48 and Remark 12.50, pp.246--247

proof.text: Compare $\phi_{x,y}$ with $\phi_{y,x}$ after switching the tensor factors. Their ratio $d$ is a regular unit on $H^2$, with $d(x,e)=d(e,y)=1$. The normalized formula of [lem-sfb-rosenlicht-product-unit-factorization] over $\bar k$ gives $d(x,y)=d(x,e)d(e,y)/d(e,e)=1$. Descend this equality by the same coefficient injection $R\hookrightarrow R\otimes_k\bar k$. Hence $*$ is commutative. This uses product-unit rigidity, not the false assertion that every regular unit on a semiabelian variety is constant.

source.place: I Proposition 8.4 and Section 9, Proposition 9.2, printed pp.35--36 and 41; agent generalization to semiabelian groups using Milne iAG2017 Proposition 12.48 and Remark 12.50, pp.246--247

proof.text: Pull back $\phi$ along $x\mapsto(x,-x)$ and identify $T_e$ with $k$ by $u$. This is a perfect rank-one pairing $T_x\otimes T_{-x}\simeq k$. Given a frame $v$ of $T_x$, let $j(v)$ be the unique frame of $T_{-x}$ paired with $v$ to $1$. Locally, in bases of these two lines, the pairing has unit coefficient $f(x)$ and $v$ has unit coordinate $t$, so $j(v)$ has coordinate $(f(x)t)^{-1}$. This is regular on the frame scheme; uniqueness makes the formulas agree on overlaps. Thus $j:E\to E$ is a morphism and $v*j(v)=u$; commutativity gives the other inverse identity. Together with the preceding steps this is a commutative group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: I Proposition 8.4 and Section 9, Proposition 9.2, printed pp.35--36 and 41; agent generalization to semiabelian groups using Milne iAG2017 Proposition 12.48 and Remark 12.50, pp.246--247

proof.text: The projection is a homomorphism since $*$ lies over $m$. Its fibre at $e$ consists exactly of frames of the fixed line $T_e$; the chosen $u$ identifies it, on every test scheme, with $\mathbf G_{m,k}$ by $a\mapsto au$. Bilinearity and normalization give $(au)*v=av$ and $(au)*(bu)=ab\,u$, so this embedding is a homomorphism and its action is exactly the specified scalar action. Finally every map $U\to H$ admits a Zariski cover trivializing the pulled-back line; a basis on each open is a lift to $E$. Such covers are fppf covers by [lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf]. Hence $E\to H$ is an epimorphism of fppf sheaves, and the displayed kernel calculation proves exactness of the asserted sequence.
